Package com.signalwire.sdk.runtime.lambda

Class LambdaAgentHandler

java.lang.Object
com.signalwire.sdk.runtime.lambda.LambdaAgentHandler
public final class LambdaAgentHandler extends Object
AWS Lambda adapter for a SignalWire AgentBase.

Translates API Gateway (REST v1 or HTTP v2) / Lambda Function URL events into the same dispatch logic the in-process HTTP server uses, without depending on the aws-lambda-java-events typed models at runtime (the handler accepts plain Map<String, Object> so the SDK stays dependency-light).

Usage — in your Lambda handler class: 


 public class MyHandler implements RequestHandler<Map<String, Object>, Map<String, Object>> {
     private final LambdaAgentHandler delegate;

     public MyHandler() {
         AgentBase agent = AgentBase.builder()
                 .name("my-agent")
                 .route("/")
                 .build();
         agent.setPromptText("You are helpful.");
         this.delegate = new LambdaAgentHandler(agent);
     }

     public Map<String, Object> handleRequest(Map<String, Object> event, Context ctx) {
         return delegate.handle(event).toMap();
     }
 }

The adapter dispatches based on the request path and the agent's configured route:

  • GET /<route> → returns rendered SWML
  • POST /<route>/swaig → executes the named SWAIG tool
  • POST /<route>/post_prompt → invokes the summary callback
  • POST /<route>/mcp → JSON-RPC 2.0 (if MCP enabled)
  • GET /health, /ready → health probes

All webhook URLs generated inside the SWML document are built from the Lambda's Function URL (via LambdaUrlResolver) or the SWML_PROXY_URL_BASE override, with the agent's route always layered on top. This is the same invariant the HTTP server path enforces.
